Name: Cu Chi Tunnels and Mekong Delta VIP Tour by Limousine
Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Southern Vietnam / Things to do in Ho Chi Minh City / Ho Chi Minh City Tours / Cu Chi Tunnels
Itinerary: Cu Chi Tunnels, My Tho
Itinerary Description:
Cu Chi Tunnels
Tour stars approximately at 7:45AM to 6:40PM - This VIP Day Tour from Ho Chi Minh City with Transfers by Limousine allows you to experience the history, culture, and natural beauty of Southern Vietnam in just one day.

Around 7:45am, get picked up from your hotel in center of Ho Chi Minh City and head to Cu Chi Tunnels. After 1.5 hours ride, we arrive at the tunnels where you will get a chance to learn about the fascinating history and significance of the tunnels during the Vietnam War. You will have the opportunity to crawl distances through the tunnels, and witness the intricate network of underground tunnels and traps that played a significant role in the war. You can also try your hand at shooting some of the old rifles used during the war.

After exploring the tunnels, we'll head to a local restaurant for lunch to try some of the delicious local Vietnamese cuisine (vegan food available)

My Tho
After lunch, we'll head to My Tho - the heart of the Mekong Delta region. You'll get a glimpse into the daily life of the locals as we take a boat ride down the Mekong River, where you can enjoy the picturesque scenery of the surrounding countryside.

We will then take a sampan ride through the small waterways with coconut palms lining both sides, where you can experience the rural lifestyle. Stop by at the bee house to watch locals perform traditional music while savoring fresh tropical fruits and honey tea.

We'll wrap up our day tour and head back to Ho Chi Minh City in the late afternoon, where we'll drop you off at your hotel around 6:50pm.

This is a unique opportunity to experience some of the best Southern Vietnam has to offer, with a mix of history, culture, and natural beauty all in one day.

Itinerary Description:
Hanoi Opera House
07:45-08:40 – Hotel Pick-Up
Our English-speaking tour guide will pick up guests from various hotels in Hanoi's Old Quarter, between 07:45 AM and 08:40 AM. We strive to make pick-ups as timely as possible, but due to morning traffic in the Old Quarter and the number of hotels to collect from, this time is approximate. Please be ready to help expedite the process.

Halong Bay
11:45-12:00 – Boarding the Cruise
The bus will arrive at Tuan Chau Marina and reach our pier, where our welcoming staff will be waiting for you with a big smile. For guests who have not booked transportation from Hanoi, please be at Tuan Chau International Marina by 11:45 AM.

Hon Ga Choi Island
12:00-13:30 – Lunch on Board 
The cruise departs from Tuan Chau harbor for a joyful journey to discover the beauty of the UNESCO World Heritage site, Ha Long Bay. Along the way, you will pass by the grandeur of the legendary bay with thousands of limestone islands, including Dog Rock, Duck Rock, and especially Thumb Rock – a beautiful limestone islet rising from the sea in the shape of a giant thumb. 
Enjoy a huge buffet lunch with a variety of dishes, including seafood and Vietnamese food. Vegetarian options do available in the buffet.

Sung Sot Cave
13:30-15:00 – Explore Surprising Cave (Sung Sot Cave)
We will stop at Bo Hon Island, where our tour guide will take you to Sung Sot Cave (Surprising Cave), the largest and most beautiful cave in Ha Long Bay. After about 200 steps through the forest canopy, the entrance of the cave will appear. A paradise will unfold before you. You will explore the cave for about 45 minutes before returning to the cruise. (For tourists who cannot walk much, you can stay on the cruise and relax on the sundeck.)

Hang Luon Cave
15:00-16:00 – Kayaking Luon Cave
The cruise heads to Luon Cave. Here, you can get active with kayaking (about 30 minutes) or enjoy the beautiful scenery at Hang Luon (Creepy Cave) with a rowboat, rowed by the local people of Ha Long Bay.

Ti Top Island
16:00-17:00 – Titop Island – Titop Beach – Titop Mountain
We will stop at Titop Island. On this small island, you can climb halfway up the mountain to enjoy a breathtaking panoramic view of Ha Long Bay. The spectacular sight from above provides an unforgettable experience.
Alternatively, you can relax and enjoy swimming at Titop Beach, where the clear, refreshing waters offer the perfect opportunity to cool off.

Halong Bay
17:00 - 18:00 – Sunset Party
Enjoy complimentary wine, Vietnamese tea, and fresh fruit as the sunset begins to set, painting the sky in deep reds, purples, and yellows. Relax in Jacuzzi and take in the scenery as we sail back to the harbor.

Hanoi Opera House
18:00 – 21:00 Disembark – Bus to Hanoi
We will dock at the harbor, board the buses, and travel back to Hanoi via the high-speed highway, with a quick stop halfway before continuing the journey.
The tour guide will drop you off at the front door of your chosen hotel in the Old Quarter. 
Depending on traffic conditions, the drop-off time may take a little longer. On weekends, drop-off times are often delayed due to road closures for the Walking Street.

Name: Cu Chi Tunnels & Saigon City Tour from Phu My Port
Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Southern Vietnam / Things to do in Ho Chi Minh City / Ho Chi Minh City Tours / Cu Chi Tunnels
Itinerary: Cu Chi Tunnels, Notre Dame Cathedral of Saigon, Saigon Central Post Office, War Remnants Museum, Saigon Opera House (Ho Chi Minh Municipal Theater), People's Committee Building, The Independence Palace
Itinerary Description:
Cu Chi Tunnels
Arrive in Cu Chi tunnels and tour guide will give you an overview introduction of Cu Chi Tunnels and its legendary history. Enjoy the scenic drive northwest towards the Cambodian border. You will get to explore a section of the network of some 125 miles (200 kilometers) of subterranean passages and rooms. Upon arrival at the Cu Chi Tunnels, take a short documentary film about the Cu Chi tunnels tell you how about the tunnels histories and how fierce the war happened. Then the tour guide will help you to learn the pivotal part they played in the war such as trap doors, and climb inside to see where the Viet Cong built storage facilities, weapons factories, kitchens. Afterward travelers can try local special foods like rice tapioca and hot tea which was main food in Cu Chi during the war. Visitors can try to fire off an AK47 or MK16 or machine guns at the nearby shooting range (not included, participate at own expense and risk).

Notre Dame Cathedral of Saigon
The Notre Dame Cathedral and the  Saigon Old Post Office. Designed by Gustave Eiffel and built between 1877 and 1883, the Post Office truly reflects classical French colonial architecture style. We finish our day with some shopping time at the Ben Thanh Market, a very popular tourist spot mainly due to its rich history and prime location. It offers a wide selection of goods ranging from faux Nike shoes to beautiful silk Ao Dai. After that, we will return to the port in good time for cruising.

Saigon Central Post Office
The Central Post Office in Ho Chi Minh is a beautifully preserved remnant of French colonial times and perhaps the grandest post office in all of Southeast Asia. Located next door to Notre Dame Cathedral, the two cultural sites can be visited together and offers visitors a chance to imagine life in Vietnam during the times of the Indochinese Empire. The building was designed by Alfred Foulhoux and features arched windows and wooden shutters, just as it would have in its heyday in the late 19th Century.

War Remnants Museum
The War Remnants Museum in Ho Chi Minh City first opened to the public in 1975. Once known as the ‘Museum of American War Crimes’, it's a shocking reminder of the long and brutal Vietnam War. Graphic photographs and American military equipment are on display. There's a helicopter with rocket launchers, a tank, a fighter plane, a single-seater attack aircraft. You can also see a conventional bomb that weighs at 6,800kg. American troops had used these weapons against the Vietnamese between 1945 and 1975.

Saigon Opera House (Ho Chi Minh Municipal Theater)
The Saigon Opera House in Ho Chi Minh is an elegant colonial building at the intersection of Le Loi and Dong Khoi Street in District 1, very close to the famous Notre Dame Cathedral and the classic Central Post Office. The restored three-storey 800-seat Opera House was built in 1897 and is used for staging not only opera but also a wide range of performing arts including ballet, musical concerts, Vietnamese traditional dance and plays. Performances are advertised around the building and information can be found in the state-operated tourist information centre close by.

People's Committee Building
The People’s Committee Building Saigon in central Ho Chi Minh City features well-preserved French colonial architecture in a spacious garden landscape. Originally constructed as a hotel in 1898 by French architect Gardes, it now serves as a city hall and one of the city’s most iconic landmarks. Occupying the end of Nguyen Hue walking promenade, it has three buildings with embossed statues of animals and people, intricate bas-reliefs on the walls, as well as a statue of Ho Chi Minh in front of the main building. The best time to visit is in the evening, as these features are beautifully illuminated with LED lights.

The Independence Palace
Independence Palace was the base of Vietnamese General Ngo Dinh Diem until his death in 1963. It made its name in global history in 1975. A tank belonging to the North Vietnamese Army crashed through its main gate, ending the Vietnam War. Today, it's a must-visit for tourists in Ho Chi Minh City. The palace is like a time capsule frozen in 1975. You can see two of the original tanks used in the capture of the palace parked in the grounds. Independence Palace was the home and workplace of the French Governor of Cochin-China. It has lush gardens, secret rooms, antique furniture, and a command bunker. It's still in use to host important occasions in Ho Chi Minh, including APEC summits.

Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Southern Vietnam / Things to do in Con Son / Con Son Tours / Bus Tours
Itinerary: Bai Biển Vung Tau, White Palace, Jesus Christ Statue, Thich Ca Phat Dai, The Whale Temple Vung Tau
Itinerary Description:
Bai Biển Vung Tau
Pick up at the port and depart to Vung Tau beach where you can relax and enjoy some fun under the sun.

White Palace
Bach Dinh, or the White Palace of Vung Tau City is located at 4 Tran Phu Street, on the slop of Big Mountain. Standing 50 meter above the sea level, White Palace has its French name which is La Villa Blanche.

Jesus Christ Statue
The 32 meter high Statue of Jesus that sits atop of a small mountain overlooking the sea (The Nui Nho). You can see the statue of Christ the King, one of the important symbols of Vung Tau, from all directions in the city. But the best is still climbing to the top of Little Mountain and admire the statue. Then, climb the observatory in the statue and watch the panorama of the city and the surrounding sea.

Thich Ca Phat Dai
Thich Ca Phat Dai (Platform of Shakyamuni Buddha) is a notable Theravada Buddhist temple in the coastal city of Vung Tau in southern Vietnam. It lies to the northwest of the Lon mountain and was built between 1961 and 1963 when it was opened. It is set on a plot of around five hectares, with a Zen Buddhist monastery at the foot of the plot and the Thích Ca Phật Đài at the top.

The Whale Temple Vung Tau
Lying on the right of the Thang Tam’s Holy Temple, the Whale Tomb was built at the same time as the Temple of the Five Eliments at the end of the 19th century. The Tomb presently displays a huge skeleton of a whale collected by the local fishermen over a hundred years ago.

Name: Tay Ninh – Cao Dai & Ba Den Mountain + Optional Cu Chi Tunnels
Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Southern Vietnam / Things to do in Ho Chi Minh City / Ho Chi Minh City Tours / Nature and Wildlife Tours
Itinerary: Ho Chi Minh City, Black Virgin Mountain, Cao Dai Temple, Tay Ninh, Cu Chi Tunnels, Ho Chi Minh City
Itinerary Description:
Ho Chi Minh City
07:00 am – Pick-up from Hotel: Our guide and driver will meet you at your hotel in Ho Chi Minh City. The tour begins with a drive to the Tay Ninh, located approximately 3 hours from the city center.

Black Virgin Mountain
we will travel to Ba Den Mountain, the highest peak in southern Vietnam. Upon arrival, take a scenic cable car ride to the summit, where you’ll be rewarded with panoramic views of the countryside, rice fields, and the distant border with Cambodia. At the peak, visit the tallest bronze Buddha statue in Asia and enjoy the stunning natural surroundings.

Cao Dai Temple
we head to Cao Dai Temple, a stunning architectural site in Tay Ninh, around 2 hours from Cu Chi. The temple is the center of Caodaism, a unique religion in Vietnam that worships the “Eye of God” and combines elements of Buddhism, Christianity, Taoism, and Confucianism. You will explore the temple’s vibrant and symbolic design and learn about its beliefs and practices. You’ll also have the opportunity to witness the noon ceremony, where followers gather to pray.

Tay Ninh
Enjoy a delicious lunch at a local restaurant, offering authentic Vietnamese cuisine.

Cu Chi Tunnels
Upon arrival, explore the Cu Chi Tunnels, a 200 km network of underground tunnels that served as a base for the Viet Cong during the Vietnam War. You’ll discover secret underground rooms, including hospitals, weapon factories, and command centers. Learn about the survival tactics of the Viet Cong soldiers, and even try a sample of cassava, a staple food they ate during the war, served with tea.

Ho Chi Minh City
We will begin the journey back to Ho Chi Minh City. You will arrive around 07:00 - 07:30 pm, depending on traffic.

End of Tour.

Name: 1 Hour Saigon River Tour in Ho Chi Minh
Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Southern Vietnam / Things to do in Ho Chi Minh City / Ho Chi Minh City Tours / Day Cruises
Itinerary: Saigon River, Hotel Majestic Saigon, Tran Hung Dao Statue, Nguyen Hue Street, Thu Ngu Flagpole, Ho Chi Minh City Customs Department, State Bank of Vietnam - HCMC Office, Mong Bridge, rạch Bến Nghé, Sài Gòn River Tunnel, Ho Chi Minh Communism Museum, Tan Son Nhat, Thủ Thiêm Bridge, Bitexco Financial Tower, Đền Quan Lớn Đệ Tam, Vietcombank Tower Saigon, Bộ Tư Lệnh Hải Quân Phía Nam, Cau Ba Son, Landmark 81, Cầu Sài Gòn
Itinerary Description:
Saigon River
A 1 hour boat tour through the heart of Ho Chi Minh City also know as Saigon. During the trip you will cruise on the Saigon River along the central district 1 and district 4 and pass by new high rise towers as well as some of the best preserved buildings of the city.

Hotel Majestic Saigon
Located at 1 Dong Khoi Street, this luxury hotel was built in 1925 in a classical French Riviera style by a wealthy local businessman.

Tran Hung Dao Statue
The statue of Tran Hung Dao (1231), a Vietnamese royal prince, statesman and military commander. Tran Hung Dao is famed for successfully stopping several Mongol invasions.

Nguyen Hue Street
This boulevard name after emperor Nguyen Hue (1753) is one of Saigon's largest boulevards and a walking street running from the Saigon River to the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City (City Hall).

Thu Ngu Flagpole
Originally built in 1865 the flagpole served as a signal mast for incoming ships. Today's version was constructed in 1900 and carries the Vietnamese flag.

Ho Chi Minh City Customs Department
Built in 1867 as a mansion to a wealthy business man, the building was converted into its current day status in 1881 and serves as the headquarters of the customs department.

State Bank of Vietnam - HCMC Office
Built in 1928 for the Banque de l'Indochine, this building now houses the Saigon branch of the State Bank of Vietnam.

Mong Bridge
One of the oldest bridges in Saigon and built by the company once led by Gustave Eiffel.

rạch Bến Nghé
Ben Nghe channel is a waterway on Ho Chi Minh City and used to be a center of commerce due to its location.

Sài Gòn River Tunnel
The Thu Thiem Tunnel is the first and only tunnel under the Saigon River and is part of an important highway.

Ho Chi Minh Communism Museum
One of the oldest buildings in ho Chi Minh City, built in 1862. The building used to be the original port and is now home to the Ho Chi Minh museum.

Tan Son Nhat
Home to the Saigon port. District 4 is an island located between the Saigon River and two canals and is Ho Chi Minh City's densest neighborhood.

Thủ Thiêm Bridge
Thu Thiem originally a largely uninhabited swampland will become Ho Chi Minh City's most modern district with residential areas, offices and large parks.

Bitexco Financial Tower
At its completion in 2010, Bitexco Tower was the tallest skyscraper in Vietnam. It's design has been inspired by the lotus flower, the national flower of Vietnam.

Đền Quan Lớn Đệ Tam
A temple on the Saigon River bank and one of the very few surviving old buildings in Thu Thiem.

Vietcombank Tower Saigon
An iconic skyscraper in Vietnam housing many national and international companies and the Vietcombank.

Bộ Tư Lệnh Hải Quân Phía Nam
A historic building on the Saigon river housing the Southern Naval Command Office.

Cau Ba Son
The latest addition to bridges spanning the Saigon River and named after the Ba Son Shipyard.

Landmark 81
Vietnam's tallest skyscraper and the 2nd tallest tower in Southeast Asia.

Cầu Sài Gòn
Until 2008 the only bridge connecting the center with District 2 and a vital gateway to Ho Chi Minh City.

Name: Hue Hoi An Bus Tour Sightseeing via Hai Van Pass 4 Stops
Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Central Vietnam / Things to do in Hue / Hue Tours / Full-day Tours
Itinerary: Thanh Toan Bridge, Lap An Lagoon, Hai Van Pass, The Marble Mountains
Itinerary Description:
Thanh Toan Bridge
1st STOP: Hue to Thanh Toan tiled bridge, estimated arrival time: 09:00 stopping time 25 minutes
Thanh Toan tiled bridge is a wooden arch bridge with a tiled roof spanning a ditch in Thanh Thuy Chanh village, Thuy Thanh commune, Huong Thuy town, Thua Thien Hue province, about 8 km east of Hue city. This wooden bridge is classified as rare and has the highest artistic value among ancient bridges in Vietnam. The bridge was recognized by the Ministry of Culture as a national cultural relic according to Decision No. 575QD/VH dated July 14, 1990.

Lap An Lagoon
2nd STOP: Thanh Toan bridge to Lap An Lagoon, estimated arrival time: 10:30 stopping time 25 minutes
Lap An Lagoon (also known as An Cu Lagoon, An Cu Lagoon or Lang Co Lagoon) is a brackish water lagoon located next to Phu Gia Pass, on the shore of Lang Co Bay, in Lang Co town, Phu Loc district, Thua Thien Hue province. This is one of 12 typical lagoons of Central Vietnam.

Hai Van Pass
3rd STOP: Lap An Lagoon to Hai Van Pass, estimated arrival time: 11:15 stopping time 25 minutes
Hai Van Pass is also called Ai Van Pass (because there was a gate at the top of the pass) or May Pass (because the top of the pass is often covered with clouds), 500 m (1640 ft) high (above sea level). , 20 km long, cutting across the Bach Ma mountain range (part of the Truong Son range running close to the sea) between the border of Thua Thien Hue province (in the north) and Da Nang city (in the south), Vietnam South.
Hai Van Gate
Today, at the top of Hai Van Pass there are still traces of a gate. This gate is called Hai Van Quan (海雲關), built in the Tran dynasty and restored in the Nguyen dynasty (the 7th year of Minh Mang, 1826), we will discover at here within 25 mins

The Marble Mountains
4th STOP: Hai Van Pass to Marble Mountain (Ngu Hanh Son), estimated arrival time: 12:30 stopping time 25 minutes
Ngu Hanh Son (Marble Mountain) or Non Nuoc Mountain is a scenic spot consisting of 5 limestone mountains rising on a coastal sandy beach, on an area of ​​about 2 km² located far from the center of Da Nang city, Vietnam. South about 8 km to the Southeast, right on the Da Nang - Hoi An route; Now belongs to Hoa Hai ward, Ngu Hanh Son district, Da Nang city. Ngu Hanh Son includes the mountains: Moc Son, Thuy Son (the largest, highest and most beautiful), Tho Son, Kim Son and Hoa Son (two peaks are Duong Hoa Son and Am Hoa Son).
Note: The remaining time is for the round tour and time spent sightseeing or explorations.
After sightseeing, we get on the bus and the bus will drop Travelers off at each your hotels in Hoi An. Estimated drop off time 14:30.

Name: Hang Pygmy Exploration 2 Days 1 Night
Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Central Vietnam / Central Vietnam Tours / Overnight Tours
Itinerary: Phong Nha
Itinerary Description:
Phong Nha
Starting at the Jungle Boss headquarters we will brief you and the team on what to expect, and check that everyone is prepared.
After the briefing we will make the 45min-1 hour ride in Phong Nha – Ke Bang National Park to the trailhead.
After saying goodbye to the last piece of humanity we will exit the road and begin the jungle hike. While walking through the jungle our guide will teach you about some local plant life, maybe feed you some tasty treats the jungle has to offer and show you some pieces of the minority people’s (the Ruc Ca Roong) culture -the Jungle people who survive off of the jungle resources.
Then, you have been supplied with filtered locally sourced water, helmet and headlamp the team will begin exploring the hang Over cave. Hang Over begins with a long narrow shaft with various cave formations, growing in size and beauty with each step. Eventually, the team will reach a massive grotto, filled with amazing stalagmites and stalactites, speleothems (decorations), and beautiful pools. Here in the grotto the guide will choose an appropriate location for lunch. After eating some cucumber salad and other snacks next to some amazing cave features you will proceed to the exit of Hang Over (see photo gallery for more!)

Hang Over and Hang Pygmy was once one large cave that experienced a ceiling collapse, creating 2 caves and a healthy unique jungle inside the cave system! After making the short jungle climb through the doline (the collapse) you will come to the massive chamber of Hang Pygmy. Here our guide and porter team will equip you with appropriate abseiling safety gear, brief you on safety procedures, and rig your harness with a fail safe system. Taking turns, one by one everyone in the company will descend into the bottom of the cavern, an 80 meter descent, with 23 meters done via abseiling. Once everyone is safely on the floor of the chamber the group will make a short walk, and turn the corner to the MASSIVE cathedral like exit of Hang Pygmy.
Pygmy cave, the fourth largest cave in the world where you will set up the campsite at the mouth of the cave or in the middle of the jungle inside the cave. While you are exploring this massive cave, our team of porters will prepare a hardy Vietnamese meal with rice, veggies, soup, and meat. Oh, and customary of Vietnamese culture, rice wine will be included, Cheers!; “Mot Hi Ba Zo!”

Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Northern Vietnam / Things to do in Hanoi / Hanoi Tours / Street Food Tours
Itinerary: Street Food Tours Hanoi
Itinerary Description:
Street Food Tours Hanoi
The tour guide will welcome you at your hotel lobby, then start the walking tour in the old quarter '36 streets' to visit some famous and specialized food stalls and local restaurants. You will watch as it is made and taste some particular dishes (The company can customize vegetarian food or something for other special requirements).

The old quarter in Hanoi is over one thousand years old and today retains much of the old flavor that made the area special in earlier times. Each street was the exclusive domain of one trade (guilds) so there are whole streets of blacksmiths, silver shops, paper shops, headstone makers and more. Originally there were just 36 streets in the old quarter but today there are more than 50. Although many of the streets are short, and the area is rather compact.

It can be very difficult to find local food on your own in the hidden alleys or sidewalks, certainly the best way to experience street food is with a local. In this special tour learn about Vietnamese cuisine, culture, people and language.

You will have a unique experience trying the foods of the local Hanoi people; the food is handled hygienically and comfortable venues are provide for the tastings. The benefit also goes back to the vendors or restaurants / families as the food is bought directly from them.

Later, the guide will bring you to enjoy a Water Puppet show which is a unique variation on the ancient Asia puppet tradition, and is a Vietnamese tradition dating back to the 11th century. Supported by a large rod placed under the water and manipulated by experienced puppeteers, the wooden puppets appear to be dancing over the water, telling folk tales. It’s entertaining and suitable for all audiences.

At the end of your Hanoi tour you are free to continue exploring the area or your guide will assist you with directions or a taxi back to your hotel.

Itinerary Description:
Cu Chi Tunnels
7:30am: Your guide will pick you up from your hotel and transport you to Cu Chi Tunnel in a mini van. The journey will take approximately one and a half hours.

As you travel along the road, you will be surrounded by serene rural landscapes, with rice paddies, rivers, ducks, and water buffalos. It may be difficult to imagine the destruction and devastation that once plagued this area due to bombings and mines, when Cu Chi was considered a "Free Target Zone." However, the remnants you will witness in Cu Chi serve as evidence of the fierce battleground that once existed there. Have you ever wondered what it's like to fire an AK-47? By visiting Cu Chi tunnels, you will have the opportunity to find out!

In the afternoon, we will depart from Cu Chi and head to My Tho City, a journey of approximately two hours by car. Along the way, we will make a stop at a restaurant for lunch.

My Tho
Upon reaching My Tho City, you will be taken on a boat ride along a small canal, which offers a serene escape from the bustling town. Cruising through the canal surrounded by coconut trees, the boat will lead you to a coconut island in Ben Tre. Once there, you will disembark and leisurely explore the village, with a stop at a local family's home. Here, you can indulge in tropical fruits, savor honey tea and honey wine, and be enthralled by traditional Vietnamese music performed by the villagers.

You will come across a coconut candy shop, where you can learn the art of candy-making and admire various handicrafts created from coconut trees. Taking a leisurely walk through the village, you will encounter a multitude of fruits, flowers, trees, and charming local houses, all while being greeted by the cheerful presence of children in the Mekong Delta.

The tour concludes at your hotel at approximately 19:00.

Itinerary: Tran Quoc Pagoda, Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, Hanoi Train Street, Temple of Literature & National University, Hanoi Old Quarter Vietnam, French Quarter
Itinerary Description:
Tran Quoc Pagoda
Begin your journey with a hassle-free pick-up from your hotel or accommodation in Hanoi’s Old Quarter, setting the stage for an exciting exploration of the city. 
Start your first visit at Hanoi’s oldest pagoda, Tran Quoc Pagoda. Constructed during the 6th century under Emperor Ly Nam Đe, this over 1,500-year-old landmark is steeped in history and spiritual significance, located on the tranquil West Lake.

Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
During the tour, we will pass by the historic Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and stop at the surrounding Ba Dinh Square for a brief introduction and photo opportunity. Please note that this tour does not include entry inside the mausoleum. If you wish to visit inside, proper clothing is required (long pants and covered shoulders). Alternatively, you may choose to visit the nearby One Pillar Pagoda, one of Hanoi’s most unique and iconic temples.

Hanoi Train Street
Experience the unique atmosphere of Hanoi Train Street, one of the most fascinating and unusual places in the city. This narrow railway runs just inches from local homes and cafés, where daily life unfolds along the tracks. Enjoy a drink at a small café while waiting for the train to pass by—an unforgettable moment that perfectly captures the charm and excitement of Hanoi.

Temple of Literature & National University
Explore the peaceful charm of Temple of Literature, the first university of Vietnam founded in 1070. With its beautiful traditional courtyards, ancient architecture, and stone steles honoring generations of scholars, this historic site offers visitors a meaningful glimpse into Vietnam’s long tradition of education and culture.

Hanoi Old Quarter Vietnam
Discover the vibrant charm of Hanoi Old Quarter, the historic heart of the city with over 1,000 years of history. Wander through its maze of narrow streets, each once dedicated to a traditional trade, where ancient houses, lively markets, street food stalls, and local life create an unforgettable atmosphere. A visit here reveals the true spirit and timeless culture of Hanoi

French Quarter
The tour will pass through Hanoi’s charming French Quarter, where you will see elegant colonial architecture such as the Hanoi Opera House, the famous Hoan Kiem Lake, and St. Joseph's Cathedral. There will be a short stop along the way so you can take photos and enjoy the beautiful scenery. The tour then ends with a transfer back to your hotel.

Itinerary Description:
Notre Dame Cathedral of Saigon
Your trip will start with a first stop at the Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon and you will get to take a lot of photos at this beautiful Church. It is the most impressive cathedral in Vietnam. Modeled on Notre-Dame de Paris and built with materials shipped over from France, the cathedral is the religious center for Vietnam’s 6.2 million Catholics.

Saigon Central Post Office
The next stop is at Saigon Central Post Office. It is one of the most iconic Instagrammable destinations in Ho Chi Minh City. With the charming colonial architecture and ornate decorations, it's a perfect spot for your social media photos. Moreover, it is a beautiful remnant of Vietnam’s complicated past. If you’re looking for an Instagrammable spot with the amazing architecture, this is definitely the place to do it.

Tan Dinh Church
Tan Dinh Church or the famous PINK Church is one of the most underrated sights in the city. Its intense color is hard to miss, and the interior is equally as stunning. During Tan Dinh’s 1929 reconstruction, wealthy parishioner Francois Haasz and his Vietnamese wife generously decorated the inside with Italian marble, creating a rich, elegant feel. To add a historical dimension to Tan Dinh, the founder of the church, Father Donatien Eveillard, is buried beneath the nave.

Ho Chi Minh City Museum
On the next destination, we'll take you to a Hidden Weapons Bunker that you wouldn't be able to find anywhere else in Saigon. You will be able to pick up and checkout actual weapons that were used during the Vietnam war.

Ho Chi Minh Square (Quảng truờng Hồ Chi Minh)
The City Hall is an architectural masterpiece completed in 1908 and still functions as a government office, so you cannot go inside. Yet you can appreciate the beauty of the structure from the outside as it looms at the north end of the pedestrian street, Nguyen Hue. The cream and yellow structure get lit up with floodlights come nighttime and is a spectacular sight, also a perfect spot for Instagram photos during the day.

Bitexco Financial Tower
Get a perfect view of the Bitexco Financial Tower while walking on Nguyen Hue Street and it's definitely an Instagramable spot.

Phap Viện Minh Dang Quang
Minh Dang Quang Pagoda is one of the largest temples in Ho Chi Minh City, established by the Mendicant Buddhist Order, one of the biggest Buddhist sects in southern Vietnam. The central octagon-shaped temple topped with a lotus flower was designed in traditional Chinese architectural style.

Saigon Opera House (Ho Chi Minh Municipal Theater)
We'll pass by this beautiful Opera House during the trip

The Independence Palace
Pass by this place during the trip

Ho Chi Minh City Museum
Pass by this famous War museum during the trip

Golden Dragon Water Puppet Theater
Pass by the water puppet theater during the trip

Cu Chi Tunnels
The tunnels of Củ Chi are an immense network of connecting tunnels located in the Củ Chi District of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, and are part of a much larger network of tunnels that underlie much of the country. The Củ Chi tunnels were the location of several military campaigns during the Vietnam War, and were the Viet Cong's base of operations for the Tết Offensive in 1968.

War Remnants Museum
The War Remnants Museum is a war museum at 28 Vo Van Tan, in District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It contains exhibits relating to the First Indochina War and the Vietnam War.

Bitexco Financial Tower
Bitexco Financial Tower is a skyscraper in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. At its completion in 2010, it became the tallest building in Vietnam and kept this status until January 2011, when it was surpassed by Keangnam Hanoi Landmark Tower. With 68 floors above ground and three basements, the building has a height of 262.5 metres, making it the second tallest building in the city, fifth tallest in Vietnam, and the 263rd tallest in the world, as of the beginning of 2018.

Ben Thanh Market
Bến Thành Market is located in the center of Hồ Chí Minh City, Vietnam in District 1. The market is one of the earliest surviving structures in Saigon and an important symbol of the city. Ben Thanh Market is a famous destination for many local and foreign tourists from all around the world. The market operates all year round and opens at around 6am} every day until the official closing time at 6pm.

People's Committee Building
Ho Chi Minh City Hall or Saigon City Hall or Hôtel de Ville de Saïgon was built in 1902–1908 in a French colonial style for the then city of Saigon. It was renamed after 1975 as Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee. Although this elegant colonial building is not open to the public, Saigon City Hall is popular for its great photo opportunities. Tourists can take photographs outside and many people choose to do this at night when the building and its grounds are lit up

Ho Chi Minh City Museum
Gia Long Palace, now officially the Hồ Chí Minh City Museum is a historical site and museum in Hồ Chí Minh City, Vietnam. The museum is situated at the corner of Lý Tự Trọng and Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa streets, located on 2 hectares of land, near the Independence Palace.

Saigon Skydeck
Enclosed observation deck for views

Emperor Jade Pagoda
The Jade Emperor Pagoda is a Taoist pagoda located at 73 Mai Thi Luu Street, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. It was built by the Chinese community in 1909. It is also known from 1984 by the new Chinese name Phước Hải Tự, and as the Tortoise Pagoda. U.S. President Barack Obama paid a visit to the pagoda during his state trip to Vietnam on 22 May 2016.

Tan Dinh Church
Tân Định church is a Roman Catholic church in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Its formal name is the Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Even though it's in District 3, the parish shares its name with neighbouring District 1's Tân Định Ward. It was built during the French colonial period in the 1870s and completed on 16 December 1876, when Vietnam was part of French Indochina.

Itinerary Description:
Black Virgin Mountain
07:00 AM – Begin your journey with a hotel pick-up and drive northeast to Black Lady Mountain (Núi Bà Đen), the highest peak in Southern Vietnam at 986 meters.

Cable Car Ride: Soar above lush forests, sparkling waterfalls, and mysterious caves on a modern cable car, taking in sweeping views of the mountain landscape.

Temples & Caves: Explore sacred temples, peaceful pagodas, and hidden caves once home to Buddhist monks and nuns. The serene spiritual atmosphere blends beautifully with the natural scenery.

Conquering Black Lady Mountain is not just an adventure but also a cultural and spiritual experience, offering breathtaking landscapes and unforgettable memories.

Cao Dai Temple
Next, visit the extraordinary Cao Dai Temple in Tay Ninh, often described as a “Walt Disney fantasia of the East.” Its exterior dazzles with bright colors, where multi-shaped dragons twist around columns and sacred symbols decorate every corner. Above the main entrance, the striking image of the all-seeing holy eye represents the unity of the Cao Dai faith. Inside, the temple is just as fascinating: statues of Jesus Christ, Buddha, and the Hindu god Brahma stand side by side, reflecting the religion’s unique blend of beliefs. The vibrant mix of colors, elaborate architecture, and spiritual atmosphere create a setting that feels both beautiful and surreal to Western visitors. A highlight not to be missed is the midday service, when hundreds of worshippers in white robes gather in prayer, offering a moving and unforgettable glimpse into the rituals of this remarkable faith.

Cu Chi Tunnels
After lunch, continue to the legendary Cu Chi Tunnels, one of Vietnam’s must-visit historic sites. This vast underground network once played a crucial role in the Vietnam War, showcasing the ingenuity of guerrilla warfare. Discover the smart design of trap doors, hidden entrances, and living chambers that allowed thousands of fighters to survive bombings and remain undetected. Despite heavy attacks, including 30-ton B-52 bombs, the area resisted capture by 30,000 U.S. troops. Here, you’ll have the unique chance to crawl through a section of the 121-kilometer tunnel system, experiencing firsthand the resilience and determination of the Vietnamese. Learn how guerrillas concealed smoke from their cooking, adapted to life underground for days, and turned the jungle into a stronghold. For an extra thrill, you can even fire real AK-47 rifles at the shooting range. The day ends as we return to Ho Chi Minh City around 6:00–7:00 PM, concluding an unforgettable journey of history and adventure.

Halong Bay
11:45-12:00 – Boarding the Cruise
The bus will arrive at Tuan Chau Marina and reach our pier, where our welcoming staff will be waiting for you with a big smile. For guests who have not booked transportation from Hanoi, please be at Tuan Chau International Marina by 11:45 AM.

Hon Ga Choi Island
12:00-13:30 – Lunch on Board 
The cruise departs from Tuan Chau harbor for a joyful journey to discover the beauty of the UNESCO World Heritage site, Ha Long Bay. Along the way, you will pass by the grandeur of the legendary bay with thousands of limestone islands, including Dog Rock, Duck Rock, and especially Thumb Rock – a beautiful limestone islet rising from the sea in the shape of a giant thumb. 
Enjoy a huge buffet lunch with a variety of dishes, including seafood and Vietnamese food. Vegetarian options do available in the buffet.

Sung Sot Cave
13:30-14:30 – Explore Surprising Cave (Sung Sot Cave)
We will stop at Bo Hon Island, where our tour guide will take you to Sung Sot Cave (Surprising Cave), the largest and most beautiful cave in Ha Long Bay. After about 200 steps through the forest canopy, the entrance of the cave will appear. A paradise will unfold before you. You will explore the cave for about 45 minutes before returning to the cruise. (For tourists who cannot walk much, you can stay on the cruise and relax on the sundeck.)

Hang Luon Cave
14:30-15:30 – Kayaking Luon Cave
The cruise heads to Luon Cave. Here, you can get active with kayaking (about 30 minutes) or enjoy the beautiful scenery at Hang Luon (Creepy Cave) with a rowboat, rowed by the local people of Ha Long Bay.

Ti Top Island
15:30-17:00 – Titop Island – Titop Beach – Titop Mountain
We will stop at Titop Island. On this small island, you can climb halfway up the mountain to enjoy a breathtaking panoramic view of Ha Long Bay. The spectacular sight from above provides an unforgettable experience.
Alternatively, you can relax and enjoy swimming at Titop Beach, where the clear, refreshing waters offer the perfect opportunity to cool off.

Halong Bay
16:30 – Sunset Party
Enjoy complimentary wine, Vietnamese tea, and fresh fruit as the sunset begins to set, painting the sky in deep reds, purples, and yellows. Relax and take in the scenery as we sail back to the harbor.

Hanoi Opera House

We will dock at the harbor, board the buses, and travel back to Hanoi via the high-speed highway, with a quick stop halfway before continuing the journey.
20:30-21:00 – Hotel Drop

Itinerary Description:
Sapa
08:00 - 08:30: Pick up at Sapa town and start the trip 
The local guide will meet you at the meeting point in Sapa town, provide a brief introduction to the journey and guide you through some necessary trekking skills, re-check the necessary things to travel.

Y Linh Ho
08:30 - 09:00: Start trekking from Sapa town, walk to the Southeast along Muong Hoa valley.
The first village is Y Linh Ho village - a village of the Black H'mong people, learn about the life, culture of the H'mong people and the wild natural scenery here.
The road to the village is usually a small trail, passing through terraced fields and majestic mountains. This road can be a bit steep, but in return is the poetic scenery of mountains and forests and simple wooden houses. At Y Linh Ho, you will see vast terraced fields, especially beautiful in the golden rice season (August) or the flooding season (May) or green rice fields (from June to July). This is an ideal place to take photos, observe the daily activities of the people and admire the rice fields with their characteristic terraced structure.

Lao Chai
10:30 - 11:00 : Continue trekking to Lao Chai village
Go 3 km further to Lao Chai village - a large village of the Black H'mong people. Cross the small bridge to enter Muong Hoa valley, enjoy the peaceful scenery of the valley.
To reach this village, our local guide will lead you through the rice terraces with the local road few tourists and up a bit so that you can see the nice view of Muong Hoa valley.
From above, you will see terraced fields stretching along the hillsides and winding along the Muong Hoa stream. Lao Chai has many stops for visitors to sightsee and take photos.

Lao Chai
12:00 - 12:30: Have lunch with local food in the restaurant in Lao Chai village near the river.
Try the local food or if you would like to have a picnic lunch on the uphill to chill the countryside atmosphere, the road we take you will have interesting places to enjoy.

Ta Van Village
13:30 - 14:00: Walk to see Ta Van village with the large rice terraces and interact with Giáy people - a popular minority ethnic in Ta Van. 
After lunch, continue trekking about 3 km to Ta Van village - home to the Giay ethnic group.
Discover the daily life, culture and traditional costumes of the Giay people, different from the H'Mong people in Y Linh Ho and Lao Chai. This is a quite famous village for tourists, because the families here have homestay services, allowing guests to stay and experience local life.
Ta Van has a very special landscape, with the Muong Hoa stream flowing through the village. The traditional stilt houses of the Giay people are interspersed with terraced rice fields, creating a peaceful and poetic picture of the countryside.

Ta Van
15:30: Arrive at local homestay or local house of minority ethnic people, overnight here 1 night to enjoy the village night.
After all day trekking hard, you will have time to relax and this time to have a talk together, deeply understanding about the life in the village, and listen to nature sounds from the countryside. Refill energy for the next day with full power.

Itinerary Description:
The Marble Mountains
Marble Mountains Danang is a group of five limestone mountains in Vietnam. This destination is not only a tourist attraction but also a Buddha worship site. Marble Mountains is a natural masterpiece bestowed to the land of Da Nang. With the harmonious beauty of the ecological area and the spiritual and cultural life, this destination attracts a lot of visitors. According to Cham legend, one day a dragon flew to Non Nuoc beach and laid an egg there. After a long time, the egg hatched and a beautiful girl stepped out of the egg. The egg shell was broken into 5 pieces that became the five magical mountains as we see today. In 1825, emperor Minh Mang named this mountain complex Marble Mountains, which means “Ngu Hanh Son” in Vietnamese. Each mountain was named after one of the five elements of Eastern philosophy: metal, water, fire, wood, and earth. These names remain unchanged until now, and Marble Mountains have become a natural attraction with many majestic peaks, caves, and temples.

This pass is not only connected with numerous historical events, but it is also a wonderful place for many travelers due to its spectacular and artistic beauty that captivates everyone’s heart. The perilous death curve, together with zigzag roads, will create a challenging trek for backpackers and bring incredibly unique experiences.

Name: From Hanoi: Full-Day Ninh Binh Highlights Small Group Tour
Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Northern Vietnam / Things to do in Hanoi / Hanoi Tours / Day Trips
Itinerary: Old Quarter, Hoa Lu Temple, Mua Caves, Tam Cốc-Bich Dộng, Bich Dong Pagoda
Itinerary Description:
Old Quarter
Between 07h15 AM to 7h45 AM : Get picked up by our friendly guide then depart for Ninh Binh province where about 100km away Hanoi Old Quarter. It takes about 2 hours drive includes breal time on the way.

Hoa Lu Temple
First stop at Hoa Lu Ancient Capital which is located in Ninh Binh provice, the land has both marvelous mountains and seas with the development of many attractive tourist areas. The ancient citadel, perhaps, makes the province more attractive because it creates the cultural identity of the area and help people understand more about the cultural, architectural and sculptural values associated with the legend about the foundation of Dai Co Viet ( an old name of Viet Nam country).

Mua Caves
Next stop to Mua Cave (Dancing Cave) and enjoy the breathtaking panoramic river and mountains view by climb 500 steps up tp Lying Dragon Mountain. Mua Cave is located at the foot of Mua Mountain. According to folk legend, upon coming back to the area for his military campaign, King Tran Thai Tong (1st King of the Tran Dynasty in Vietnam) usually came to this cave to enjoy all the songs and dances performed by his odalisques. That’s why people call it Mua Cave - which means the cave of dances or the dancing cave. People now use the name Mua Cave to refer to the whole tourist area around it.

Tam Cốc-Bich Dộng
Enjoy set-menu lunch with traditional Vietnamese dishes. After lunch, guests enjoy a sampan boat trip in Tam Coc, passing through three caves: Hang Ca- Frist cave, Hang Hai the second cave and Hang Ba- third Cave. Then keep cycling through the rice fields and villages to visit Bich Dong Pagoda.

Bich Dong Pagoda
Last stop at Bich Dong Pagoda which was built in 1428. It is famous for not only its beautiful and charming scenery, but also being a place historical relics of Ninh Binh province.

At the end of the day, guests will say goodbye Ninh Binh and get on our tourist bus to return Ha Noi between 19h00 PM to 19h15 PM and drop off at your hotel in Ha Noi Old Quarter. Tour finish!

Cai Rang Floating Market
Arrive at the ferry to Visit the Floating Market:
We will begin the tour at a traditional local market, simple and friendly, where you can experience the authentic charm of the area, enjoy the beautiful sunrise over the Mekong River.

Visit Cai Rang Floating Market (The largest floating market in Vietnam)
Cai Rang Market is a must-see when visiting Can Tho. Enjoy a traditional local breakfast, including coffee, coconut water, and other options like vegetarian meals.

Take a ride on a large local boat where locals sell agricultural products. You’ll also have the chance to enjoy fresh fruits (included in the tour).

Sông Cần Thơ
Explore Beautiful Canals
Discover the scenic canals that contribute to Can Tho’s reputation as one of the world’s most beautiful canal cities. You can enjoy the peaceful surroundings of lush green trees and mangrove palm-lined water ways.

Binh Thuy Ancient House
Return to the ferry and continue the exciting journey ahead. On the way, we will have the opportunity to explore Binh Thuy Ancient House, a historic house that is over a century old.

Cồn Sơn
A small boat will take us to a tropical island in the heart of the Mekong River, where we will enjoy various activities with the local people:
- Take a scenic trek through the Mekong countryside and its beautiful islands 
- Experience making traditional Vietnamese cakes 
- Discover lush orchards filled with pomelo and star apple trees 
- Enjoy a traditional lunch with a local family 
- Indulge in a delightful cake buffet 
- Watch the captivating snakehead fish dance, a unique local recreational activity 
- Visit a floating fish raft village and learn about this fascinating way of life

Ho Chi Minh City
End an exciting journey where you’ll have nearly explored all of Can Tho in just one day.

Itinerary: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, Temple of Literature & National University, Vua Chả Cá - 269 Giảng Võ, Hai Ba Trung Temple, Long Bien Bridge, Hidden Gem Cafe Hanoi
Itinerary Description:
Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
Part 1: Hanoi Highlights: (2 hours) You will be greeted by the tour guide and driver at your hotel lobby we then ride to Ho Chi Minh Complex to have a quick visit to Ho chi Minh mausoleum – the Mecca of Vietnamese, Ba Dinh square, Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh Residential area and One Pillar Pagoda.

Temple of Literature & National University
After Ho Chi Minh Complex, we move to Temple Of Literature, a 1000 year-old iconic architecture of Hanoi to learn about Vietnamese long-standing culture and history.

Vua Chả Cá - 269 Giảng Võ
Despite the famous TRAIN STREET of Hanoi recently has been CLOSED by the local government, we know exactly HOW, WHEN & WHERE to take you there to wait for and capture the fun moments of the day by sitting by the train street cafe and watching the train passing by. We guarantee that TRAIN STREET is a part of our trip.

Hai Ba Trung Temple
Part 2: Hanoi Hidden Gems: (2,5 hours)

Explore the parts-unknown of Hanoi by riding through the maze of zigzagging backstreet and narrow alleyways and markets. Diving into the rivers of motorbikes and Hanoi street symphony. Traveling with all your senses heightened: Watching, Hearing, Touching, Tasting and smiling. Experiencing the GOOD, the BAD, and the WEIRD of the city as it is what it is. Experiencing different slides of life behind the scene, the hidden part of the iceberg. Meeting people where they live, work, learn and pray. Building personal connections and culture exchanges.

*Note: Hai Ba Trung Temple is the area where we visit, so you could easily get the idea about the part of Hanoi that we visit, NOT necessary to come in more Temple on the trip.

Long Bien Bridge
Long Biên Bridge is the oldest iron bridge in Vietnam, built in 1889 by French colonial, was imbued with national identity even though it was a modern architectural heritage at that time, as the French gave it the shape that resembles a dragon flying over the Red River, which is associated with the cultural symbol of Hà Nội. A short walk here gives you a great angle of Hanoi for photos and we also take you to the countryside of Hanoi to explore the peaceful and tranquil villages and farms around the city.

Hidden Gem Cafe Hanoi
A quaint little coffee shop in the heart of Hanoi Old Quarter. All furniture is creatively made from cycled materials. Serving authentic & organic Vietnamese coffee and drinks. It is a truly hidden gem of Hanoi where we chill out and have best egg coffee before riding back to the hotel.

Golden Dragon Water Puppet Theater
Visit: Golden Dragon Water Puppet Theater, Ho Chi Minh City

Generations ago, Vietnamese puppeteers performed for their rural communities in waist-deep water, bringing to life legends and stories about their region. Water puppetry theaters like Golden Dragon Water Puppet Theater continue that tradition into the modern day and are a fun, family-friendly way to experience a hallmark of traditional Vietnamese culture.

With the entrance ticket you have the chance to relish in the fascinating art of a water puppet show, which is closely associated with the spiritual life of Vietnamese people, especially in the countryside. The show’s chosen stage is the surface of a water pool. The puppeteers present their clever skills in managing puppets by long bamboo rods and string mechanism under the surface. A traditional Vietnamese orchestra is an excellent music accompaniment.

The puppets depict the story from the songs during the show, which reflects the peaceful life of the Vietnamese countryside, so it is not too difficult to understand it.

Itinerary Description:
Tam Cốc-Bich Dộng
Tam Coc Boat Trip
Glide along the Ngo Dong River through stunning limestone karsts and peaceful rice paddies. Pass by riverside villages while enjoying the serene countryside scenery.

Bich Dong Pagoda
Begin with a visit to Bích Động Pagoda, a tranquil temple complex set within limestone mountains, where you’ll explore ancient pagodas and enjoy sweeping views of lush rice fields and karst landscapes.

Vai Gioi Cave
Vái Giời Cave (Heaven Praying Cave)
Located atop a mountain, Vái Giời Cave is known as a sacred place where ancient people once came to pray for good weather and peace. Inside the massive cave chamber, you'll find stunning stalactites and stalagmites that have formed over millions of years. The climb is a bit steep—but the panoramic views and spiritual atmosphere are worth every step.

Mermaid Cave
Tiên Cá Cave (Mermaid Cave)
Steeped in local legend, this enchanting cave is named after a mythical mermaid said to have lived here. As you walk along its narrow, winding paths, marvel at the shimmering rock formations that resemble underwater scenes—adding a touch of fantasy to your journey underground.

Thung Nham Ecotourism Zone - Ninh Binh
Next, head to Thung Nham Bird Park, a peaceful nature reserve known for its diverse bird species. Enjoy a relaxing boat ride through verdant wetlands, caves, and forests, and experience the spectacular sight of thousands of birds returning to roost.
Your journey continues with visits to the mystical caves of Vái Giời (Heaven Praying Cave), Tiên Cá (Mermaid Cave), and Hang Bụt (Buddha Cave). Please note that access to these caves may be restricted during heavy rains or flooding to ensure visitor safety.

Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Northern Vietnam / Things to do in Hanoi / Hanoi Tours / Hanoi Old Quarter
Itinerary: Lake of the Restored Sword (Hoan Kiem Lake), Old Quarter, Thang Long Water Puppet
Itinerary Description:
Lake of the Restored Sword (Hoan Kiem Lake)
The tale goes that Le Loi King came across a shining metal bar when he visited his friend. It turned out that his friend caught the bar in one of his attempts for fish. The King asked for the bar, brought it home and moulded it into a sword. All of a sudden, there was two words printed on the sword “Thuan Thien” (harmonious with heaven).

Le Loi then understood that the sword was a gift from heaven. He used it for the battle against the war with a neighbouring country. At the beginning of 1428, when peace prevailed, on one of his trip to the Thuy Quan (now Hoan Kiem) Lake, there was a tortoise rising above water and shouting: “Please return the sword to the Dragon King”. Without hesitation, the King threw the sword to the lake. The tortoise took the sword and dove down the water. From then on, Thuy Quan became Hoan Kiem lake.

Old Quarter
Located in the middle of Ha Noi, a rapidly developing city where changes take place every hour, Ha Noi Old Quarter with its old-styled narrow streets full of antique brick houses seems to nostalgically resist the flow of time while still actively trying to adapt to the dynamic atmosphere of the modern city.

Once a bustling area where merchants and artisans gathered to sell their products, Ha Noi Old Quarter consists of many small, meandering streets, each bears the name of the goods that was specifically traded there such as Hang Bac (Silver Product), Hang Ma (Paper Product), Hang Go (Wood Product), just to name a few.

Visiting this unique historical vestige comfortably lying around Hoan Kiem Lake, tourists get lost in a totally different world from the rest of the city and have the chance to explore the modest but energetic life of the local a hundred years ago, where there were no high-rise buildings, too much traffic or fancy stores; things will get a little bit smaller, as visitors may have used to those skyscrapers and shopping centers in other parts of the city, but not at all less lively and vigorous.

Thang Long Water Puppet
Located at 57B, Dinh Tien Hoang street, nearby Hoan Kiem Lake, Thang Long Water Puppet Theater is a familiar address for both domestic tourists and foreign ones, who want to enjoy water puppet shows and discovery the beauty of this unique Vietnam traditional art.

In 1969, the theater was established and since 1990; many water puppet shows have been performed by Thang Long theater artists.Every year, about 500 shows are offered to approximately 150,000 audiences. Moreover, the theater has brought water puppetry art to more then 40 foreign countries like Japan, France, America, Australia, Spain… through performance tours, or international cultural exchange program or puppetry festivals.

Name: Private Jeep Tour Saigon by Night: Foodie & City Tour
Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Southern Vietnam / Things to do in Ho Chi Minh City / Ho Chi Minh City Tours / Saigon Opera House (Opéra de Saïgon)
Itinerary: The Independence Palace, Saigon Opera House (Ho Chi Minh Municipal Theater), Saigon Notre Dame Cathedral, Ho Thi Ky Flower Market
Itinerary Description:
The Independence Palace
The Jeep will takes you to The Reunification Palace, also known as Independence Palace, is listed as a historical monument by witnessing great changes of Ho Chi Minh City’s history (formerly known Saigon) and having in itself the essence of Eastern culture. Throughout the heroic battles, this amazing work of architecture had witnessed almost every high and low of the Vietnamese war.

Saigon Opera House (Ho Chi Minh Municipal Theater)
The Saigon Opera House was custom built in 1897 by the French architect Eugene Ferret. It is one of the top venues in Vietnam to listen to opera and classical music.

Saigon Notre Dame Cathedral
Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon is a cathedral located in the downtown of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Established by French colonists who initially named it Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Saïgon, the cathedral was constructed between 1863 and 1880. It has two bell towers, reaching a height of 58 meters (190 feet).

Ho Thi Ky Flower Market
Located on a street of the same name, Ho Thi Ky is the largest flower market in Ho Chi Minh City, supplies flowers to the city and some provinces in the South of Vietnam. Founded in the 1980s, this is a rare place that upholds the characteristic of the old Saigon.

Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Central Vietnam / Things to do in Da Lat / Da Lat Tours / Bus Tours
Itinerary: Elephant  Waterfall ( Thac Voi), Pongour Falls, Lâm Hà District Police, Cuong Hoan Silk Factory, Trại dế Thiện An, Me Linh Coffee Garden, Vạn Thành, Linh An Pagoda
Itinerary Description:
Elephant  Waterfall ( Thac Voi)
One of the most Powerful Waterfall in Dalat, discover the windy cave under the waterfall.
***Due to the waterfall's operational issue, Elephant waterfall is temporarily closed. However, we are still able to enjoy the whole view of this breath-taking waterfall from Linh An pagoda (a close distance)

Pongour Falls
Among various waterfalls in Dalat such as Datanl, Elephant, Pongour, surrounded with a huge unspoiled forest, definitely stands out.

It is about 40 m high, 100 m wide. Its polished steps look like a natural amphitheater! A stream of water powerfully plunges down these seven staircases, filling the air with a loud sound. The waterfall is imposing, but not formidable. Its beauty is poetic and praised by the locals as well as tourists.

Lâm Hà District Police
Tanung village ( the village of minority ethnic ) - One of the small groups of Chil People who live in Dalat at the beginning when Dalat's foundation and development. K'ho people group live in the valley nearby Falls and the river

Cuong Hoan Silk Factory
The silk weaving factory in Dalat is an interesting place to visit, to see the entire process, from cocoon to the fabric. This is the only silk factory in the country that maintains the old method of removing silks from the cocoons. The cocoons are soaked in hot water, and the delicate thread is wound onto a machine that unravels the cocoon. The thread is then wound onto a reel, which is used on a large loom, to weave it into a delicately patterned fabric.

Trại dế Thiện An
Tourists coming here are guided by the farm owner on how to raise crickets, care for crickets, breed… Moreover, visitors can also enjoy dishes made from crickets..

Me Linh Coffee Garden
Located about 23km from the center of Da Lat to the southwest and have to cross the beautiful Ta Nung winding pass. Me Linh Coffee plantation – enjoying the original weasel coffee (self-sufficient),

Vạn Thành
Known as Dalat's largest flower village. Although steep terrain, in the form of stairs, this is still the main flower supply for Dalat, especially roses. Van Thanh Rose is known for the body of wild roses. With the new rosebud imported from the Netherlands, the people of Van Thanh have created many kinds of roses of different colors such as pink velvet, pink lotus, pink roses, yellow moonlight, and pink .... strong roses, this place also attracts many visitors through many beautiful flowers such as daisies, glasses, Salem, carnations, coins ... Lac step in the "kingdom of flowers", visitors also enjoy the charming scent.

Linh An Pagoda
Linh An Tu is one of the architectural works of Da Lat. This is a temple with ancient architectural works of Da Lat city. When visiting this place, visitors will be ecstatic with its beauty

My Son Sanctuary
We will begin our day trip by visiting My Son, the capital and religious center of the former Champa Kingdom, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Nestled in a lush green valley, My Son features dozens of red brick towers and sanctuaries dating from the 7th to the 13th century. After exploring this historic site, we will enjoy lunch at a local restaurant.

The Marble Mountains
In the afternoon, we will discover the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son), meaning “Five Elements Mountains.” Here, you will have the opportunity to explore stunning natural caves and enjoy breathtaking views from the mountain’s summit. The Linh Ung Pagoda, located within the Marble Mountains, has been designated a national historical and cultural site by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism.
We will also visit Am Phu Cave, where you can experience a replica of “Heaven and Hell.” Listen for the echo of bats’ wings as you contemplate the mysterious pagodas and nearby sculpting village.

Linh Ung Pagoda
Finally, we will head to the Son Tra Peninsula to visit the impressive Son Tra Linh Ung Pagoda, the largest pagoda in Da Nang City, known for its architectural grandeur and serene atmosphere.

Itinerary Description:
Ba Na Hills SunWorld
At Sun World Ba Na Hills, travelers can enjoy the famous Golden Bridge held by giant hands, ride the scenic cable car, explore French-style villages, visit beautiful gardens and pagodas, enjoy fun theme park games, and experience cool mountain weather with stunning views.

Golden Bridge
The Golden Bridge in Ba Na Hills is one of Vietnam’s most iconic wonders—an unforgettable walkway seemingly lifted by two giant stone hands above the clouds. With panoramic mountain views and magical photo spots, it’s a must-visit highlight that travelers from all over the world come to experience.

Dragon Bridge
The Dragon Bridge is a bridge over the River Han at Da Nang, Vietnam.

The Marble Mountains
The Marble Mountains are home to several Buddhist and Hindu grottoes. A stairway of 156 steps leads to the summit of Thuy Son, the only Marble Mountain accessible to visitors. It allows a wide panoramic view of the surrounding area and the other marble mountains. There are a number of grottoes, including Huyen Khong and Tang Chon, and many Hindu and Buddhist sanctuaries, the temples of Tam Thai, Tu Tam and Linh Ung, and the pagoda of Pho Dong. The sanctuaries feature statues and relief depictions of religious scenes carved out of the marble

Lady Buddha
People in Son Tra Peninsula recalled that, at the time of Minh Mang King (Nguyen Dynasty, XIX century), there was a Buddha statue from nowhere to drift on the sandbank here. Believing that was an auspicious sign, people here established a shrine for worship, from that, the region was stable and fishermen could work in peace during a long time. The sandbank where the Buddha statue drifted was then named Bai But (i.e. Buddha land on earth) also was where Ling Ung pagoda erected today

Saigon Opera House (Ho Chi Minh Municipal Theater)
The Saigon Opera House, a stunning architectural gem in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City, stands as a testament to the city's rich cultural heritage and vibrant arts scene. Built in 1897 by French architect Eugène Ferret, this magnificent edifice boasts an exquisite blend of French colonial and Renaissance architectural styles. Its elegant façade, adorned with intricate carvings and statues, draws visitors into a world of artistic splendor. Inside, the opulent interior, featuring grand staircases, chandeliers, and plush seating, provides an ideal setting for a variety of performances, from classical concerts and ballets to modern theatrical productions. Located on the bustling Dong Khoi Street, the Saigon Opera House not only serves as a cultural hub but also as a historical landmark, offering a glimpse into the city's colonial past while celebrating its contemporary artistic spirit.

Ben Nghe Cruise
Experience the magic of Ho Chi Minh City with an unforgettable dinner cruise along the Saigon River. As the cityscape transforms into a dazzling display of lights, step aboard a luxurious vessel where a culinary adventure awaits. Savor an exquisite multi-course meal featuring a fusion of Vietnamese and international flavors, all while gliding past iconic landmarks like the Bitexco Financial Tower and the historic Saigon Port. The gentle breeze and panoramic views provide the perfect backdrop for an enchanting evening. Live traditional music and dance performances enhance the ambiance, creating a feast for the senses. Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or simply seeking a unique way to explore the city's vibrant nightlife, a dinner cruise offers an unparalleled blend of romance, culture, and gourmet dining. This river voyage promises a memorable and serene escape from the city's hustle and bustle, allowing you to see Ho Chi Minh City from a fresh and captivating perspective.

Held in a pool of water that serves as the stage, these performances bring to life traditional folktales and legends through intricately crafted wooden puppets. Manipulated by skilled puppeteers hidden behind a bamboo screen, the puppets dance, swim, and act out scenes of rural life, mythical creatures, and historical events. Accompanied by live traditional music, including drums, gongs, and bamboo flutes, and narrated by expressive folk singers, the show offers an auditory and visual feast. The reflection of the puppets on the water, combined with vibrant colors and dramatic lighting, creates a magical atmosphere that delights audiences of all ages. District 3 Tax Department

District 3 Tax Department
Try sticky rice
Sample grilled sticky rice banana with coconut milk.

Hòa Bình District 10 Cultural Center
Wander through tiny alleyways to a local vendor serving crispy giant "Bánh Xèo" and bite-sized "Bánh Khọt". Southern-style rice pancakes, paired with an abundance of fresh Vietnamese herbs.

As we arrive at our first stop, you'll be greeted by the sight and aroma of sizzling pancakes being cooked right before your eyes. Our expert chef will demonstrate the art of making Banh Xeo, showcasing the technique and skill required to achieve the perfect crispiness and flavor.

You'll have the opportunity to taste both the big and small versions of this delightful dish, allowing you to compare and contrast the different textures and flavors. From the crunchy exterior to the savory filling of shrimp, pork, bean sprouts, and herbs, every bite is sure to tantalize your taste buds.

District 3 Tax Department
As we explore this historic neighborhood, you'll witness the vibrant activities of local residents going about their nightly routines, offering a glimpse into authentic Saigonese life.

Immerse yourself in the bustling atmosphere and capture stunning photos of the unique architecture and lively street scenes that characterize this area. From the colorful facades to the bustling markets, every corner offers a snapshot of Saigon's rich cultural heritage.

Hòa Bình District 10 Cultural Center
After our flavorful adventure with Vietnamese Pizza, it's time to pause and refresh ourselves with a quintessential Vietnamese drink: fresh sugar cane juice. We'll make our way to the bustling second-hand and seafood markets, where you'll find vendors expertly pressing sugar cane to extract its sweet nectar.

As we arrive at the market, you'll be greeted by the rhythmic sound of the sugar cane press and the sweet aroma that fills the air. Take a moment to catch your breath and immerse yourself in the vibrant atmosphere of this bustling marketplace.

At the juice stand, you'll watch as the vendor skillfully feeds sugar cane stalks through the press, extracting the fresh juice that's bursting with natural sweetness. The result is a refreshing and revitalizing beverage that's perfect for quenching your thirst on a hot day.

Sip on your freshly squeezed sugar cane juice and savor the pure, natural flavors that dance across your palate.

Hòa Bình District 10 Cultural Center
We explore the local area and indulge in one of Saigon's most intriguing street foods: Vietnamese Pizza. Originating from the Central Highlands area, this dish puts a creative twist on the traditional pizza concept, offering a flavor experience like no other.

Itinerary Description:

After enjoying the Floating Market trip, we will leave for the Cu Chi Legend Tunnel. The journey to the Cu Chi tunnel takes around 3.5 hours, and we will have lunch at a local restaurant on the way.

Upon arrival, you will have the opportunity to explore remnants of wartime, such as the secret bunkers used as military shelters for Vietnamese soldiers. You can watch a documentary to understand how the Vietnamese bravely fought for independence.

Visitors can crawl and crouch through the tunnels to gain insight into the challenging conditions people faced in the past. Additionally, they can visit the shooting range at their own expense (excluding bullet costs).

Before departing, you'll have the chance to sample tapioca and tea, which were staples of the soldiers' daily diet in the past.

Hanoi Food Tasting Tours
We will pick you up at your hotels within the Old Quarter or meet at our office. Here, we will provide a short briefing about our tour.

Old Quarter
During our 3-hour street food tour in Hanoi, you'll embark on a captivating journey that delves into the rich culture and history of this vibrant city. As you wander through the bustling streets, you'll be immersed in a world brimming with tantalizing street food vendors. Hanoi's street food scene is unlike that of many other major cities around the world; it's a unique culinary adventure that offers a chance to savor a diverse array of dishes from local food stands and family-run restaurants.

Our tour boasts a rotating menu, ensuring you experience the full spectrum of Hanoi's delectable options. While the specific dishes may vary from day to day, some of the mouthwatering treats you might indulge in include: savory rice noodle soup with succulent beef, flavorful rice noodle dishes featuring tender chicken or grilled pork, adventurous snail delicacies, or a hearty serving of dry noodles.

Duờng Tau
Experience the enchanting Train Street of Hanoi, even amid recent closures. Our expertise ensures a seamless visit, where you'll witness trains passing by from the Train Street cafe. This historic railway, in operation for over a century since the French colonial era, remains vital for North-South transportation. Daily life harmoniously unfolds alongside the tracks, creating a unique atmosphere. Enjoy coffee trackside for an exceptional tourist experience. Our knowledgeable guide will share intriguing stories as you witness coffee shops and houses near the tracks, making Train Street a captivating highlight of your Hanoi journey.

Old Quarter

Tags: Things to do in Vietnam / Things to do in Central Vietnam / Things to do in Da Nang / Da Nang Tours / Marble Mountains
Itinerary: My Son Sanctuary, The Marble Mountains, Linh Ung Pagoda
Itinerary Description:
My Son Sanctuary
We will begin our day trip by visiting My Son, the capital and religious center of the former Champa Kingdom, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Nestled in a lush green valley, My Son features dozens of red brick towers and sanctuaries dating from the 7th to the 13th century. After exploring this historic site, we will enjoy lunch at a local restaurant.

The Marble Mountains
In the afternoon, we will discover the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son), meaning “Five Elements Mountains.” Here, you will have the opportunity to explore stunning natural caves and enjoy breathtaking views from the mountain’s summit. The Linh Ung Pagoda, located within the Marble Mountains, has been designated a national historical and cultural site by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism.
We will also visit Am Phu Cave, where you can experience a replica of “Heaven and Hell.” Listen for the echo of bats’ wings as you contemplate the mysterious pagodas and nearby sculpting village.

Linh Ung Pagoda
Finally, we will head to the Son Tra Peninsula to visit the impressive Son Tra Linh Ung Pagoda, the largest pagoda in Da Nang City, known for its architectural grandeur and serene atmosphere.

The surrounding area of Luon Cave comprises a lot of well-known places of interest in Halong Bay. In front of Luon Cave is Con Rua Island (Turtle Island), and on the right of this cave is the Heaven Gate. Not only that but in the area of Bo Hon Island is Sung Sot Cave, which is the most magnificent cave in Halong Bay. Tien Cave and Trinh Nu Cave are also famous caves in Halong Bay in the area near Luon Cave.

Itinerary Description:
War Remnants Museum
We start the day with a visit to the War Remnants Museum, where you’ll gain a deep insight into Vietnam’s history during the war. The moving exhibits and photographs will help you understand the emotional and historical significance of this era.

Saigon Central Post Office
Marvel at the architectural beauty of the Saigon Central Post Office, an impressive colonial-era building, and the Notre-Dame Cathedral, an iconic symbol of French influence in the city.

Saigon Opera House (Ho Chi Minh Municipal Theater)
We’ll also stop by the Saigon Opera House, a stunning French colonial building that remains a cultural cornerstone of the city.

Independence Palace
Next, visit the Independence Palace, also known as the Reunification Palace, a symbol of the end of the Vietnam War. Explore its grand rooms, corridors, and historical artifacts that tell the story of this pivotal moment in history.

Nguyen Hue Street
Take a stroll along Nguyen Hue Walking Street, a bustling pedestrian boulevard where you can experience the vibrant local culture, street performances, and local cafes.

Saigon River

Sung Sot Cave
Sung Sot (Surprise) Cave: Explore The Biggest Cave in Halong Bay
A place so amazing that the French deemed it “Grotte des Surprises” or (Surprise Grotto), Sung Sot Cave is one of the biggest, most beautiful caves in Halong Bay and a highlight on most Halong Bay itineraries.
Sung Sot Cave was discovered by a French in 1901.
Elevation: 25 meters above sea level.
This is the largest and perhaps the most beautiful cave in Halong Bay with an area covering up to 10,000 sqm.
“Surprise” is the immediate feeling you may have when visiting this incredible natural artwork.
Sung Sot Cave is among the most prevalent tourist attractions for travelers and it is included in almost all itineraries of cruises exploring Halong Bay.
The cave is accessible by a rented canoe, a day cruise, or an overnight cruise.
Best time to visit: Year round; however, the best months to visit are from October to December when the humidity level is low (60-70%).

Hang Luon Cave
Luon Cave is a part of Bo Hon Island, which is about 14 kilometers from the mainland of Bai Chay City. Known as the island of amazing things, Bo Hon Island is an outstanding location in Halong Bay that most tourists choose as a nextstop on their way discovering Halong Bay.

The surrounding area of Luon Cave comprises a lot of well-known places of interest in Halong Bay. In front of Luon Cave is Con Rua Island (Turtle Island), and on the right of this cave is the Heaven Gate. Not only that, in the area of Bo Hon Island is Sung Sot Cave, which is the most magnificent cave in Halong Bay. Tien Cave and Trinh Nu Cave are also famous caves in Halong Bay in the area near Luon Cave.

Ti Top Island
Ti Top Island is preferable for tourists when taking Halong Bay tours, thanks to its ideal location. Specifically, Bo Hon Island and Sung Sot Cave are ahead of the island, while Dam Nam Island is to the right, and Cua Luc Bay is on the backside. Moreover, Ti Top Beach is located only about 7-8 kilometers away from Bai Chay Tourist Area to the Southeast.

From the bird's eye view, Ti Top has a steep slope on one side and an inclined slope on the other side. The beach coast here has a moon-like shape with the smooth white sand and is favored with stunning nature. You can find its water clear and blue all year round, thus making pebbles visible on the sandy bottom. All of these geographical factors turn Ti Top Island into a must-visit stopover in Halong Bay.
